title: Expose per-tick sandbox dispatch over HTTP from the Worker
description:
The Go orchestrator runs in a container. A container cannot create a sibling Sandbox: the binding is a Worker binding. So the container asks the factory over HTTP, and this tick is the Worker side of that call.

Do not write the machinery - it exists. cloudflare/src/sandbox-executor.ts (724 lines, from k4s) already has namedSandbox(binding, name) to resolve a Sandbox DO by name and findWorkProcess to inspect a running one, and is built around NOT carrying a live Sandbox object across a step boundary. Its only caller today is epic-reconciler.ts:1649 via sandboxExecutorFromEnv, and mn7 deletes that caller. This tick gives it a new one.

What the route must do, and the shapes matter because the Go side in the next tick builds to them:
  - start an attempt in a sandbox NAMED BY THE ATTEMPT'S IDENTITY, not by a fresh id, so a second call for the same tick+attempt finds the running one instead of starting a rival
  - report the state of a named sandbox: running, finished with a result, or absent
  - return a HANDLE, never block until the attempt finishes. Nothing waits.

Auth is not new either: e08 ported the door/container auth-challenge and the cold-start budget. Use it rather than inventing a second scheme - a route that starts compute must not be open.

Keep the HTTP contract in one place and document it there; the Go client and this route are the two consumers of one mechanism, which is the drift that 99f and mn7's own header are both about.
acceptance_criteria: A Worker route starts an attempt in a named per-tick sandbox and returns a handle without waiting, a second call with the same identity returns the SAME running attempt rather than starting a second, an unauthenticated call is refused, and the Worker test suite passes
